Hi Stephanie,

We're working through the SIG and have a few follow-ups about your incident response / breach notification section before we mark it as complete. Can you confirm the following for GreenFin's review?

- Primary point of contact for incident notifications (security + legal escalation) and phone numbers.
- Typical acknowledgement and investigation timelines (we've seen "notify within 72 hours" in other vendors — is that Redwood's threshold?).
- Which internal teams are automatically alerted (Security Ops, Legal, CS) and which require manual escalation?
- Evidence/retention windows you can provide for forensic artifacts (audit logs, commit history, VM images).
- For cross-border customers: do notification timelines differ for EU/UK/APAC?

Attached is our SIG Request v12 with the fields we couldn't map. If you can send an updated worksheet and a short explanation for the timeline POCs, that would be ideal.

Thanks — we hope to close this section by EOD Monday.

Subject: Re: SIG: incident notification & PII handling questions

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Answers below and I've attached our working SIG workbook (v3) with the specific cells filled.

High-level answers (summary):
- Primary POCs:
  - Security Engineering (incident coordination): Marcus Lin, marcus_lin@redwood.com, +1-415-555-0132
  - Legal / Escalation: Grace O'Connor, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, +1-415-555-0176
  - Customer Success (customer notifications / timelines): me, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, +1-415-555-0144

- Acknowledgement & investigation timelines:
  - Acknowledgement: automated acknowledgement to the reporter within 1 hour during business hours (we aim to acknowledge 24/7 reported incidents via our on-call rotation).
  - Initial triage: within 2 hours for incidents classified as high/critical by our monitoring/triage systems.
  - Customer notification: for confirmed customer-impacting data incidents (confirmed exfiltration or unauthorized access to customer data), we commit to notifying the affected customer(s) within 72 hours of confirmation. Note: this 72-hour window is tied to confirmation, not initial detection; it allows forensic triage to avoid false alerts.

- Automatic alerts vs manual escalation:
  - Automatic: Security Ops, On-call SRE, and the Incident Commander are automatically paged by our monitoring.
  - Manual escalation: Legal and Customer Success are looped in automatically for incidents meeting our "customer-impacting" criteria; for borderline cases Security Ops will consult Legal and CS and escalate manually.

- Evidence retention we can provide as part of an incident response:
  - Audit/log export: default retention 90 days (longer retention available by contract).
  - Application-level request logs / KV cache traces: 30 days by default.
  - Forensic VM images or full disk snapshots: retained for 30 days post-capture; permanent retention requires an approved legal request and contract addendum.

- Cross-border differences:
  - Notification windows do not change (we still follow the 72-hour customer notification policy for confirmed exfiltration), but legal/regulatory steps may differ by jurisdiction — we engage our legal counsel for EU/UK APAC specifics and will coordinate localized language and additional regulator notices as required.

I've attached: SIG_Redwood_Response_v3.xlsx (filled answers and cell-level notes) and a short customer notification template in the linked doc above. If you'd like, I can produce a GDPR-specific variant of the notification template for EU-scoped customers — let me know.

Next steps: please confirm which customers (scope) you want mapped to these answers and whether you require any additional evidence types or longer retention in the contract.

Thanks,

— Stephanie Nguyen
Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that's very helpful. A couple follow-ups before we finalize:

- PII escrow / legal hold: if there's confirmed exfiltration, will Redwood provide a secure transfer of affected artifacts to GreenFin for our forensic team or do you require Redwood to perform the primary forensic analysis? Is a signed NDA / DPA amendment required before transfer?
- Forensics timeline: 30 days for VM images is tighter than some vendors — can you confirm whether that can be extended to 90 days on request, and what the approval path looks like?
- Cross-border push notifications: we need to confirm whether Redwood will proactively notify EU data protection authorities (if required) or only provide assistance in drafting notifications — which is your standard practice?

Also — do you have an example of the customer notification text you plan to send? A single-paragraph sample would be perfect to include in our risk board notes.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Anna

Folks — forwarding GreenFin's follow-ups. I answered the baseline questions in the SIG sheet (attached) but they want clarity on three items we should confirm internally before I send the final customer-facing answers:

1) PII transfer / forensic custody: Anna asked whether we will transfer artifacts to the customer's forensic team or perform the bulk analysis internally. My read: we do analysis internally by default and provide exports under NDA; direct transfer of artifacts to customer forensics requires legal approval & a signed DPA amendment. Marcus — confirm whether we can make a 90-day retention exception on request and the operational steps to do so (storage, costs, authorization).

2) Notifications to regulators: typical play is that we coordinate and provide the draft notification and evidence packet; legal (Grace) triggers regulator outreach if required. Grace — please confirm Redwood's standard (we generally do not proactively notify regulators on the customer's behalf unless there's a contractual/regulatory obligation).

3) Customer notification sample: propose the single-paragraph template below (will send to Anna if approved):

"We are writing to inform you of a security incident that may have affected data associated with your account. Upon detection, we initiated our incident response process and have contained the activity. We are conducting a forensic investigation to determine the scope and will notify you within 72 hours of confirmation of any unauthorized access to your data. We will provide the impacted data categories, remediation steps, and recommended actions as soon as they are available.

If this wording is approved, I'll send to GreenFin and indicate that transfers of raw artifacts require an executed DPA amendment and explicit legal approval."

Please reply with quick approvals or edits. If you want me to loop in Legal Ops for signatures/NDA language I can do so.

Thanks,
Stephanie
